prompt:
A full-length figure of an enemy for the pre-fight screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration, exactly matching the game's painted backgrounds: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour, in the limited palette given below. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting or anatomy rendering, no glossy highlights, no glow, no soft gradients, no fine fur or skin detail, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art or AI art. The body is seen in three-quarter view from slightly below, angled away from the viewer, but the head is turned and the eyes look straight at the viewer, sizing them up. A relaxed, casual, confident pose, at ease and completely sure of itself: standing or leaning with its weight on one leg, its weapon resting or held loosely, not attacking, not lunging, not shouting. Menace through calm. Give it depth and volume: overlapping forms and shading washes and ink hatching that model the body in light and shadow, lit by the light of its scene (given below), as if painted into the same picture as the backdrop; still hand-drawn, never glossy, airbrushed or rendered. Only a faint, soft, semi-transparent painted shadow on the ground under the feet; no smoke, mist, dust or embers anywhere. The whole figure fits inside the frame. Cut out cleanly on a fully transparent background apart from that shadow: no scenery, no moon, sun, fire or other light source drawn in (the backdrop already has it), no frame, no text. The brush rhythm of Chinese ink-wash painting mixed into the pen-and-ink style.

Subject: The Bull Demon King of Journey to the West: a huge demon king with the head of a black bull and great curved horns, burning eyes, in red-and-gold lacquered armour and a long cape, standing tall with the iron cudgel resting across his shoulders and both hands hooked over it, chin raised, looking down at the viewer with contempt. Chinese, Ming dynasty, with the brush rhythm of Chinese painting. Light: the glow of lava from the right.
Colour: near-black iron to deep red (#140808 to #7a2a1e) with bronze, flame orange and dull gold accents.
